newsitem.title: USA: U.S spot resids steady to higher again, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S spot resids steady to higher again, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were unchanged to slightly higher Friday in light activity, with mixed forecasts clouding opinions about market direction though bloated stocks should limit the upside, traders said.

"The fundamentals seem weak. There's a lot of oil around, but some people are trying to talk the market up," said one cash trader, referring to price gains this week despite relatively mild East Coast weather and ample avails.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent gained 25 cents to $18.00-18.25 a barrel, with February paper talked little changed in the $18.00-18.25 area, traders said.

NYH 0.3 percent high pour firmed another quarter to the low-$19 area on reports a New York utility was mulling the possibility of a spot HP tender next week. Low pour notionally was steady to higher at near the $21 level.
High sulphurs in New York again were flat on the day.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent rose 25 cents to about $16.50, while three percent held steady in the high-$14s.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
Cold weather moving into the East boosted New York city gate weekend gas prices slightly to the $3.30s/mmBtu. NYH one percent resid climbed to a $2.88/mmBtu equivalent.
